orbit.title: Orbit achieved
orbit.text: The engines go quiet and the capsule glides into a steady orbit. Your crew floats free and waves at the camera. Mission Control erupts in cheers.
rosa: You did it, Flight Director. Three people are circling the Earth because of your choices.
Every part, every test and every hard call added up to this moment.
Measure twice, launch once. You measured well.
rosaNoMedal: You made it to orbit, Flight Director. Your crew is waving at you right now.
But a few shortcuts cost you points. Look at the badges you missed.
Measure twice, launch once. Next time, measure a little more.

launch_failure.title: Launch failure
launch_failure.text: The rocket couldn't finish the climb to space. The crew is safe on the ground, but the mission is over for now.
rosa: Rockets are hard. Even NASA has had launches go wrong.
The good news: your crew is safe, and now you know more than before.
Look at what shaped your odds. Then let's try again.

came_home_early.title: Home early
came_home_early.text: Your crew made it to space! Then something broke that they couldn't fix up there, so the mission ended early. They are heading home safe.
rosa: You reached space. That part went right.
Then a problem came up the crew couldn't fix. Coming home was the smart call.
Real crews have had to do this too. Safety first, then try again.

bankrupt.title: Out of money
bankrupt.text: The money ran out before launch day. The hangar lights go off and the doors close. Nobody was hurt, and the rocket waits for another day.
rosa: Running a space agency is like a long road trip. Run out of gas, and the trip ends.
Big projects need a cushion of money for surprises.
Next time, keep some money in reserve. Measure twice, launch once.
bankrupt.noPrTip: Next time, a PR lead can run a fundraiser when money gets tight.

gave_up.title: Mission called off
gave_up.text: You called off the launch. The crew is safe, and the rocket waits for another day.
rosa: Calling it off is a real Flight Director move. It takes guts.
The capsule wasn't ready, and there wasn't enough time or money to finish it.
Next time, keep the build moving on the trail so launch week starts with a full capsule.
Remember that cost review? The flag is not getting any redder.
That review was a warning light on the dashboard, and we drove right past it.
When someone checks your spending, listen. Fixing it early is cheaper.
Tasha passed the hat, and we spent the hat too.
The fundraiser bought us time, but the spending kept going.
Extra money is a second chance. Spend it like it's the last one.
We're not that rich... Leave money for the road ahead.
The build used up almost all our money before the trail even started.
Next time, pick cheaper parts where it's safe and keep a cushion for the trip.
Money doesn't grow on trees now. Save a cushion.
Every week on the trail costs money, and surprises cost even more.
Like gas money on a road trip, keep some extra for the bumps.
Congratulations, you successfully funded the launchpad's parking fees. The rocket stays on the ground.
Every day we wait costs money, and holds and scrubs cost even more.
Sometimes the first good day is the best day. Pick it and go.

window_closed.title: Window closed
window_closed.text: Day 46 came and went. The launch window shut, and the rocket stays on the ground. The crew is safe, but the mission has to wait.
rosa: A launch window is like catching a train. Miss it, and you wait for the next one.
Delays and scrubs ate up our days.
Next time, leave a few spare days for bad weather.
You took the scenic route, and the launch window left without you.
Some trail choices cost days. Those days added up fast.
When a choice costs time, ask yourself if the time is worth it.
The forecast for tomorrow looks phenomenal. Shame the mission ended today.
We waited for perfect weather, and the window closed while we waited.
A launch window is like catching a train. A good-enough day beats a missed train.

aliens.title: Secret ending found!
aliens.text: Something strange is waiting in orbit. A glowing saucer pulls alongside, and its crew starts to dance. That mysterious component was a hit!
rosa: Well. I flew for thirty years and never saw that.
I'm not sure that mysterious component was in any manual.
Measure twice, launch once... and wave back, I suppose.
